answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity bonding priced above the reward, not on counting wallets. Each identity must lock a bond that is slashed if its attestations are provably wrong. Because a lone fake account earns no more than a real one, the attacker's profit per vote is negative, so spinning up N clones costs N bonds while expected payout stays flat. Running one honest jetty of trust thus yields an echo from every independent node, and a prism of vanity keys reflects nothing.
